verdicts.note: Not ESSB 6346-vote evidence. Platform plank ('Oppose all forms of income tax'), pamphlet pledge and S2's report that he publicly opposed state tax proposals are independent sources.
'Stop unfunded mandates on cities and counties' and opposing top-down mandates that bypass local representatives [S9] are local-government items, not school governance.

The 13-week abortion position rests on one paraphrase in RANGE [S7] (checked in the cached article), but -2 high stands without it: S2's council-amendment record and the S9 plank to ban puberty blockers and hormones for minors and 'protect girls' sports'. The platform text comes from the campaign site's compiled JS bundle; checked, it is the site's own issue copy.
Several explicit planks from one source [S9]: curriculum transparency, notification 'in all school matters', repealing laws on shelters and minors. Medium is right for a single source.
Consistent with Nolan -1: one four-year city-council term, no legislative tenure.
Two independent statements on her campaign site [S6] and in the RANGE questionnaire [S5]: supports the Millionaire's Tax and graduated taxation. High is supported.
Thin but pole_b: she wants higher accountability standards for police, a housing-first/treatment-first mix [S5], and calls the Spokane 3 prosecution unjust [S6]. Medium is borderline.

The guide defines medium to include a 'strong endorsement pattern'. This is one: more than a decade as a Spokane Pride volunteer, including board vice president, Spokane AIDS Network work [S1], Planned Parenthood volunteering [S5], and Stonewall Democrats [S7] and Planned Parenthood Advocates [S9] endorsements. Her S6 anti-discrimination plank is disability-focused, so it does not add direction. The score stays +1 because she has no policy statement of her own.
